transit.pay: The MetroCard is gone — payment is now OMNY: just tap a contactless bank card or phone at the turnstile. No bank card? Buy an OMNY card for $1 at station vending machines and many shops. A ride costs $3.00, and after 12 paid taps in a week the rest are free; the Staten Island Ferry is free.
transit.hours: The subway runs 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, though late-night service is less frequent.

landmarks: Statue of Liberty

Standing tall in New York Harbor since 1886, Lady Liberty is the world's ultimate symbol of freedom and the first glimpse of America for millions of immigrants. A ferry ride out to Liberty Island offers unbeatable skyline views.
Empire State Building

This Art Deco icon has defined the Manhattan skyline since 1931, and its 86th-floor observatory delivers a jaw-dropping 360-degree panorama. At night it glows in ever-changing colors visible across the city.
Times Square
A dazzling explosion of neon billboards, Broadway marquees, and nonstop crowds, Times Square is the self-proclaimed 'Crossroads of the World.' It's chaotic, kinetic, and unmistakably New York.
Central Park
This 843-acre green oasis in the middle of Manhattan offers lakes, meadows, bridges, and skyline views that shift with every season. It's the perfect antidote to the city's concrete rush.
Brooklyn Bridge

This 19th-century engineering marvel connects Manhattan and Brooklyn with graceful stone towers and cables, offering one of the city's best pedestrian walks. Sunset crossings reveal a postcard-perfect skyline view.
One World Observatory

Atop the tallest building in the Western Hemisphere, this observatory offers sweeping views over Lower Manhattan and the harbor, built beside the solemn 9/11 Memorial. It's both a tribute and a triumph.
The Metropolitan Museum of Art

One of the world's great art encyclopedias, the Met houses everything from Egyptian temples to Impressionist masterpieces under one Fifth Avenue roof. Its grand staircase and rooftop garden are icons in their own right.
Grand Central Terminal

Beneath its celestial ceiling mural, this Beaux-Arts masterpiece has been shuttling commuters since 1913 and remains one of the world's most beautiful train stations. The whispering gallery and main concourse are must-see stops.
Rockefeller Center

Home to the Top of the Rock observation deck, the golden Prometheus statue, and the famous winter ice rink and Christmas tree, this Art Deco complex is a hub of city energy year-round. Its rooftop view rivals the Empire State's, minus the crowds.
High Line

This elevated park built on a former freight rail line winds above Chelsea's streets, lined with wildflowers, art installations, and Hudson River views. It's an unexpected slice of nature woven through industrial architecture.

train.note: Both Canada trains are daytime services from Moynihan Train Hall - bring your passport, and expect a lengthy stop at the border where officers board the train. The Adirondack to Montreal takes around 11 hours and the Maple Leaf to Toronto around 12, both far slower than flying but scenic along the Hudson and Lake Champlain. No international sleepers run from New York, but Amtrak long-distance routes like the Lake Shore Limited to Chicago offer overnight sleeper cars, and the Acela and Northeast Regional run constantly to Boston, Philadelphia and Washington. Booking opens 11 months out and Acela fares rise steeply close to departure.

bus.note: Direct daily coaches from Midtown Manhattan: Montreal about 8-9 hours, Toronto about 11-12, with both day and overnight departures. Most services use the Port Authority Bus Terminal at 42nd Street and Eighth Avenue, though some curbside operators load near Hudson Yards or Chinatown instead. Everyone gets off for passport control at the border, so pad your schedule by an hour or more. Fares are lowest booked online well in advance.

ferry.note: No international ferry sails from New York. Local boats are worth a ride though: NYC Ferry links the boroughs along the East River and out to the Rockaways for a flat fare, and the Staten Island Ferry is completely free with superb Statue of Liberty views - ignore anyone trying to sell you a ticket for it. Both run year round, with NYC Ferry services thinning out in winter and the Governors Island route seasonal. Neither carries cars; bikes are allowed on NYC Ferry for a small surcharge.
